clue.text: Collect for a service

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Someone gathers people together to attend a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate in quantity.

clue.text: A song about bad times in the plant

indicators.note: the song wraps around the other letters, so about signals one piece set inside another

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

indicators.note: bad suggests the word times is spoilt and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener sings a sad song about hard times while tending a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TEMIS (the anagram of TIMES, from 'bad') inside ARIA, after its first two letters; the leading 'A' and 'in the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic herbs and shrubs, wormwood and mugwort among them.

clue.text: The seaman a foot behind

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a rating in the navy

explanation.surface: A sailor stands a foot behind someone on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical word for towards or at the stern, so to the rear.

clue.text: Those in front rushed to bag a bird

indicators.note: to bag is to capture and hold, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to rush is to speed, past tense sped
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Hunters at the front hurry forward to shoot a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bag' puts A plus RHEA inside SPED, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The spearhead of an attack is the leading group pushing forward.

clue.text: Following strike, promise illumination

indicators.note: following says the promise comes after the strike in the answer

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
to plight one's troth is to promise

explanation.surface: After an industrial strike, workers are promised that the lights will come back on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the glow given out by a lamp, a kind of lighting.

clue.text: Young puss in form perhaps

parts.note: puss is a country name for a hare, and a hare's resting hollow in a field is called its form; the surface suggests a kitten on good form

explanation.surface: A kitten seems to be on fine form.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, and hares shelter in hollows called forms.

clue.text: Thought about one's being badly treated

indicators.note: about means the thinking wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to muse is to think, so thought is mused
one is I, and one's is I'S, written IS

explanation.surface: Someone broods over having been treated badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misused has been handled wrongly or abused.

clue.text: Night climber detected in horrible murder

indicators.note: detected in says the letters are found within the run of the words horrible murder

explanation.surface: A detective sees a nocturnal climber at the scene of a gruesome killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are tree-climbing Madagascan primates, many of them active at night.

clue.text: Making progress in one's later years

definitions.meaning: advancing or managing well, as in a career

explanation.surface: An older person is still doing well despite age.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both advancing successfully and becoming elderly.

clue.text: Free food — dug right into it

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dug is an udder or teat

explanation.surface: Someone digs straight into a free meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' looks like the past tense of dig; it is the old word for an animal's teat. 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is food or entertainment paid for by someone else, free to the guest.

clue.text: Cockney thieves in their cups?

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, a London dialect, the phrase rhymes with and stands for thieves
what is left in the bottom of teacups after drinking; in one's cups normally means drunk

explanation.surface: London crooks are drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming-slang term for robbers is also the leftover infusion found in a cup.

clue.text: This measure satisfied the engineers

parts.note: to meet a demand is to satisfy it, past tense met
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: The engineers were happy with this measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is a unit of length, a measure.

clue.text: A doctor has to right the vehicle

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor must set an overturned car upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is a car, a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Support outside transport control

indicators.note: outside says the support wraps around the transport

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for an arm
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Restraining rails are placed outside the railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts TRAIN inside REST, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control or the holding back of action.

clue.text: It could make an islet conspicuous

indicators.note: it could make says the words an islet can be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A small island can be made to stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or striking, standing out from its surroundings.

clue.text: Nauseating hot meals possibly including duck

indicators.note: including says the rearranged letters hold the extra piece
possibly suggests the words hot meals might be put together in another way

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Hot meals, perhaps with duck on the menu, turn the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HOT MEALS into LATHSOME, and 'including' puts O inside it after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means disgusting, causing revulsion.

clue.text: Man on the board given a drink

definitions.meaning: a piece in the board game ..., known as checkers in America
a swallow or measure of drink

explanation.surface: A board member is offered a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is both a counter in draughts and a single swig of liquid.

clue.text: An end to poetry? Quite the opposite

parts.note: a tip is the end of something
odes are poems

explanation.surface: Someone proposes ending poetry; another says the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. 'Quite the opposite' sounds like a retort; it defines places diametrically opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes are places on the far side of the globe, directly opposite one another.

clue.text: Over fifty in the ship are without cogs

parts.note: over can mean excessively, too

indicators.note: in says the fifty sits inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral fifty
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: Elderly passengers aboard the vessel have no teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogs are the teeth of a gearwheel, so a wheel with none is gapped of teeth.

clue.text: A prohibition put on leave

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A ban has been imposed on taking time off.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or leave behind.

clue.text: Can put up tax for salt

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
rates are a local tax

explanation.surface: A government can raise taxes on salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid.

clue.text: A pound was demanded of this merchant

definitions.text: A pound was demanded of this merchant

parts.words: A pound was demanded of this merchant
parts.note: in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, Shylock demands a pound of the title merchant's flesh; the surface suggests a cash payment

explanation.surface: A trader was asked for a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, who pledged a pound of his flesh.

clue.text: Bill gets about in, a noble- man's entourage

indicators.note: an entourage surrounds its master, so the a-and-nobleman pieces enclose the letter

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A bill about the household of a nobleman is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entourage' puts C between A and COUNT; 'gets' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a bill listing money owed.

clue.text: Catechism arranged according to plan

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of catechism are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Religious teaching is laid out systematically.
explanation.definitionFit: Schematic describes something set out as a diagram or orderly scheme.

clue.text: Backing soft floor-coverings to make an impression

indicators.note: backing means the words soft and floor-coverings are read from the end towards the start

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
mats cover floors

explanation.surface: Soft rugs underneath leave a mark on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp is to press down and leave a mark or imprint.

clue.text: Bohemian girl seen round a resort in America

indicators.note: round says the girl surrounds the other letter

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme

explanation.surface: A free-spirited young woman is spotted around an American beach town.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a Florida city known as a holiday destination.

clue.text: Area of land by Church

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A plot of land lies beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch, also called a rod or pole, is an old unit of land area.

clue.text: About mid-morning get up and wash

indicators.note: about says the getting up wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to get up is to rise

indicators.note: mid- picks the middle letter of the word morning

explanation.surface: Around midmorning someone gets out of bed and washes.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of seven-letter 'morning' is N, which goes inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with clean water.

clue.text: A ranger's sound when finding the scent

indicators.note: sound says the words are heard rather than read, giving a near-identical pronunciation

parts.note: a ranger is a roamer, one who wanders

explanation.surface: A park ranger hears something while tracking an animal's smell.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'a roamer' and the answer sound alike. 'when finding' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell, usually a pleasant one.

clue.text: A trip to get cake in plenty

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: A day out to buy plenty of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like an outing; it is a dance. 'to get' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a plentiful supply, more than enough.

clue.text: Coppers take the inmate to be a VIP

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated p
an inmate is one who lives in a place, a resident

explanation.surface: Police arrest a prisoner, who turns out to be an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police; it means copper coins. 'take the' and 'to be a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A president, as head of state, is a very important person.

clue.text: Dispenses with out-houses

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of garden outbuildings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for casting off and the plural of a garden hut.
